ei.title: Breaking the Cycle: Solutions to E-waste
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste. What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world. Right-to-Repair Movement: Empowering Consumers One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause. Repairability Index: Information at a Glance In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead. Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future. Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② hesitate → hesitating: be동사(is) 뒤 진행형이므로 -ing 형태 hesitating
det.analysis:
① cracked: 'the screen is cracked'에서 화면이 '금이 간' 상태라 be동사 뒤 수동·과거분사 cracked가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② hesitate → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'she is ___ to do so'에서 앞에 be동사 is가 있으므로 현재진행형 'be + -ing' 형태가 되어야 해요. 따라서 hesitating으로 써야 해요. 동사원형 hesitate는 be동사 뒤에 올 수 없어 틀려요. ❌ hesitate는 틀림 ←정답

③ seem: 'getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option'에서 조동사 might 뒤 동사원형 seem이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ contributing: 'she will be contributing to a serious problem'에서 'will be + -ing' 미래진행형이라 contributing이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: be동사(is) + -ing 진행형: is hesitating

✅ ② a more sustainable society(더 지속 가능한 사회): 더 적은 전자·전기 제품이 매립지에 가게 되면서 프랑스가 '더 지속 가능한 사회'로 변화할 것을 기대할 수 있다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ a fully automated world(완전히 자동화된 세계): 본문에 없는 내용
❌ ④ a completely free market(완전히 자유로운 시장): 수리 가능성 지수의 효과와 무관
det.tip: make a transition to a more sustainable society: 더 지속 가능한 사회로의 변화

questions.passage: A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead. Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 수리 가능성 지수의 특징.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a repairability index' 일치

❌ ② 본문 'Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system' 일치

❌ ③ 본문 'a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair' 일치

✅ ④ 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 본문 'The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts.'에서 이용 가능성뿐 아니라 분해의 용이성과 '여분 부품의 가격'도 고려한다고 했어요. '가격은 고려하지 않는다'는 반대예요 ←정답
det.tip: including ~ the price of spare parts(부품 가격도 고려)가 사실입니다.

ch: 2021년 1월 프랑스 정부는 수리 가능성 지수를 포함시킬 것을 요구하는 법안을 통과시켰다.
그 지수는 0에서 10 사이의 점수와 색상으로 표시되는 시스템을 사용한다.
녹색 라벨의 높은 숫자는 그 제품이 수리하기 쉽다는 것을 나타낸다.
그 지수는 수리 정보의 이용 가능성만 고려하고 부품 가격은 고려하지 않는다.

questions.passage: The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 수리 카페의 특징.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam'에서 '네덜란드'에서 열렸다고 했으므로 불일치

✅ ② 본문 'They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices'와 일치 ←정답

❌ ③ 본문 'The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts'에서 '자원봉사자' 전문가들이라고 했으므로 급여 지급·고용은 불일치

❌ ④ 본문 'there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world'에서 '30개국 이상'이라 했으므로 불일치
det.tip: free meeting places where people can gather ~ and fix(모여서 고치는 무료 장소)가 일치. 나머지는 본문과 반대입니다.

ch: 세계 최초의 수리 카페는 미국에서 2009년에 문을 열었다.
수리 카페는 사람들이 모여 고장 난 장치를 고칠 수 있는 무료 만남의 장소이다.
수리 카페는 전문 수리 기사를 고용해 급여를 지급한다.
수리 카페는 현재 전 세계 10개국 미만에 존재한다.

questions.passage: Imagine she ①<u>lived</u> in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be ②<u>limited</u> to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and ③<u>replace</u> them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have ④<u>purchase</u> a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ purchase → purchased: 'would have + 과거분사'의 가정법 과거완료이므로 purchased
det.analysis:
① lived: 'Imagine she lived in a world where ~'에서 현재 사실과 반대되는 가정을 나타내는 가정법 과거라 과거형 lived가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② limited: 'her options wouldn't be limited to ~'에서 선택지가 '제한되는' 것이라 'would be + 과거분사'의 수동태 limited가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ replace: 'She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself'에서 order와 and로 이어지는 병렬 구조라 동사원형 replace가 맞아요(able to order and (to) replace). ✅ 올바름

④ purchase → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'she likely would have ___ a laptop'에서 'would have + 과거분사'의 가정법 과거완료예요. 따라서 과거분사 purchased로 써야 해요. 동사원형 purchase는 틀려요. ❌ purchase는 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료 would have + 과거분사: would have purchased

questions.passage: What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 전자 쓰레기(e-waste)는 버려진 전자 장치(discarded electronic devices)와 더불어 무엇을 가리키는지, 그 대상을 나타내는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 전자 쓰레기가 가리키는 대상.
det.analysis: 본문 'The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances.'에서 전자 쓰레기는 버려진 전자 장치와 '전기 기기(electrical appliances)'를 가리킨다고 했다. 따라서 답은 electrical appliances이다.
det.tip: discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances에서 electrical appliances를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. det.korean: 수리 카페가 연장할 수 있게 하는 것.
det.analysis: 본문 'Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans.'에서 수리 카페는 개인이 장치를 유지하고 그것의 '수명(life spans)'을 연장할 수 있게 한다고 했다. 따라서 답은 life spans이다.
det.tip: maintain their devices and extend their life spans에서 life spans를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people __________ (sign) up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: signing (with + 목적어 + 분사).
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'with more and more people ___ up to volunteer'는 'with + 목적어(people) + 분사'의 부대상황 구문이다. 사람들이 '신청하는' 능동의 의미이므로 현재분사 -ing를 써야 한다. 따라서 sign을 signing으로 바꿔야 한다. 'with more and more people signing up(점점 더 많은 사람이 신청하면서)'으로 해석된다.
det.tip: with + 목적어(people) + 현재분사(signing): ~가 …하면서

questions.passage: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 소재.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 노트북 수리점을 고르는 방법은 Liz 예시의 일부일 뿐 주제가 아님

❌ ② 프랑스 정부의 가격 규제가 아니라 '수리 가능성 지수' 법안이며 전체 주제도 아님

❌ ③ 자원봉사자의 어려움은 본문에 없는 내용

✅ ④ 글은 수리할 권리 운동, 수리 가능성 지수, 수리 카페 등 전자 쓰레기를 줄이기 위한 전 세계의 다양한 수리 관련 해결책을 다룸 ← 정답
det.tip: 수리할 권리 운동·수리 가능성 지수·수리 카페를 관통하는 것이 주제입니다.

ch: 노트북이 고장 났을 때 수리점을 고르는 효과적인 방법
프랑스 정부가 가전제품 가격을 규제하게 된 역사적 배경
자원봉사자들이 수리 카페를 운영하며 겪는 어려움과 그 극복 사례
전자 쓰레기 문제를 줄이기 위한 전 세계의 다양한 수리 관련 해결책들

questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글쓴이가 전하려는 핵심 메시지.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문은 전자 쓰레기 문제를 해결하려는 노력을 강조하므로 '신경 쓸 필요 없다'는 반대

❌ ② 본문은 수리가 더 지속 가능한 선택임을 보여주므로 '새 제품 구입이 항상 더 경제적'은 반대

❌ ④ 본문은 소비자·지역 사회·기업·정부 모두의 노력을 다루므로 '정부만'은 반대
det.tip: 제품을 수리하기 쉽게 만들어 전자 쓰레기를 줄이려는 노력이 확산되고 있다는 것이 요지입니다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"이 문제를 다루기 위해 노력이 이루어지고 있다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) address, are, being, efforts, made, problem, this, to 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: efforts are being made to address this problem
det.analysis:
주어는 '노력' efforts예요. '이루어지고 있다'는 '만들어지고 있는 중'이라는 현재진행 수동태 'be동사 + being + 과거분사'로 써요: are + being + made.

'이 문제를 다루기 위해'는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사로 이어요: to + address + this + problem.

순서대로 이으면 efforts / are / being / made / to / address / this / problem (8단어)이에요.
det.tip: 현재진행 수동태 are being made + 목적의 to address: ~을 다루기 위해 노력이 이루어지고 있다

questions.wa: efforts are being made to address this problem
